summary_en: Hirogin Holdings raised FY2027 annual dividend per share by 7 yen to 77 yen, comprising interim dividend of 38.50 yen (up 3.50 yen) and year-end dividend forecast of 38.50 yen (up 3.50 yen), based on upwardly revised profit forecast and 40% payout ratio policy.
title_en: Notice Regarding Revision of Earnings Forecast for FY2027 (Full Year Ended March 31, 2027) and Decision on Interim Dividend and Revision of Year-End Dividend Forecast (Dividend Increase)
translation_en_brief:
Hirogin Holdings raised its full-year dividend per share for FY2027 (year ended March 31, 2027) by 7 yen to 77 yen. The interim dividend was increased by 3.50 yen to 38.50 yen as of September 30, 2026, and the year-end dividend forecast was raised by 3.50 yen to 38.50 yen. This brings the projected payout ratio to 40.4%.

The dividend increase follows an upward revision of the full-year profit forecast. Consolidated net income attributable to parent company shareholders is now projected at 56.5 billion yen, up 10.8% from the previous guidance of 51.0 billion yen, and earnings per share are forecast at 190.50 yen versus 172.73 yen previously. The improvement reflects higher-than-expected gains in lending interest income and securities dividend income at Hiroshima Bank, the holding company's subsidiary.

The company stated its basic shareholder return policy aims to implement dividends in line with consolidated net income while maintaining adequate internal reserves, targeting a payout ratio of approximately 40%. The increase aligns with this principle following the revised profit outlook.
